emergency.note: Non-emergency police is 114 and the capital region's urgent medical helpline is 1813; operators speak English.

hood_landmark.Norrebro: Assistens Cemetery, the leafy resting place of H.C. Andersen
hood_landmark.Osterbro: The Little Mermaid statue on the Langelinie waterfront
hood_landmark.Christianshavn: Freetown Christiania's murals and alternative community
hood_landmark.Frederiksberg: Frederiksberg Gardens and its canal-side palace views

avoid.reason: Very safe; buy nothing on Pusher Street in Christiania (drug-trade tensions); usual pickpocket caution

hood_desc: Norrebro is Copenhagen's most multicultural and edgy district, packed with independent cafes, ethnic eateries and buzzing nightlife around Jaegersborggade and Superkilen park, it suits students, young creatives and anyone drawn to a diverse, energetic vibe.

Vesterbro is a gritty-turned-trendy quarter centered on the hip Meatpacking District, full of craft bars, coffee shops and design boutiques, it appeals to young professionals and nightlife lovers who want an urban, bohemian scene close to the Central Station.

Osterbro is a leafy, affluent and family-friendly neighborhood near the lakes, Faelledparken and the harbor baths, with wide streets and calm residential charm, it suits families and well-off professionals wanting a quieter, upscale setting.

Christianshavn is a picturesque waterfront district laced with canals, houseboats and cobbled streets, home to Freetown Christiania and a laid-back bohemian feel, it appeals to those wanting a charming, characterful area within walking distance of the center.

Frederiksberg is an elegant, green and prosperous independent enclave known for its gardens, tree-lined avenues and stately apartments, it is ideal for families and affluent residents seeking a refined, peaceful lifestyle near the city core.

water.note: Tap water is untreated groundwater and considered among the best-tasting and safest in Europe.

transit.pay: Buy single tickets (from DKK 24 / ~US$3.80) at station and airport machines, or use the Rejsekort app to check in and out with your phone - the old physical Rejsekort card is being phased out in favor of the app. The City Pass (from DKK 100 / ~US$16 for 24 hours) covers metro, trains, buses and harbour buses including the airport. One ticket is valid across all operators.
transit.hours: The Metro runs 24/7. S-trains and buses run about 5am-12:30am, with all-night S-trains and night buses on Friday and Saturday nights.

transit.m: Metro M2 to Norreport/Kongens Nytorv (~15 min)
DSB regional train to Central Station (~13 min)
